Subject: BlueRiver - quick ask: control plane / egress proof for SIG

Marissa,

Thanks for the SOC 2 packet last week — that helped. We're now working through the SIG questionnaire and the security team wants a concise architecture rationale specifically for Dedicated/Private inference deployments. Two concrete asks: a one-page diagram that highlights tenant fencing and control-plane separation, and a mapping table that ties those controls back to SIG/CAIQ question IDs (or the comparable control names).

Can Redwood provide a short "control fence playbook" (diagram + bullets) and a prefilled SIG worksheet we can use in our internal review? Ideally by Wednesday so we can include it in our audit packet.

Appreciate it — Javier
Javier Lopez
Head of Security Engineering, BlueRiver Systems
security@blueriver.com

From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
To: Javier Lopez <javier.lopez@blueriver.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com, tessa_morgan@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: BlueRiver - quick ask: control plane / egress proof for SIG

Javier — thanks for the clarity, and absolutely. Attaching a short playbook and a diagram export; we can also drop a prefilled SIG workbook. High level notes included inline below so your reviewers have context without digging into the diagram: 

- Isolation model: Dedicated pools are enforced at the compute layer by namespace and VPC segmentation; Private (VPC) deployments add customer-managed subnets with route-level ACLs and a hardened control-plane proxy.
- Control plane separation: management APIs and model-serving data plane live on distinct network planes. Control plane traffic is limited to our control proxies (outbound-only from customer VPC) and authenticated with mutual TLS + KMS-backed client certs.
- Egress controls: default deny, explicit NAT / proxy paths for telemetry endpoints; customer-configurable egress allowlists for external integrations.
- Tenant fencing proof points: per-tenant KV cache scoping, ordered instance allocation (no cross-tenant shared process), and per-request tenant IDs enforced in the runtime layer with audit hooks.
- SIG mapping: we've flagged the most common CAIQ questions and included where each artifact (diagram, ACL list, cert rotation notes, audit logs) satisfies the ask.

I attached: redwood-control-fence-playbook-v1.pdf, network-diagram-tenant-overlay-v2.png, and a starter SIG responses sheet.

Next steps I propose: Kimberly to provide the CAIQ cell mapping; Tessa to add the operational runbook excerpt for certificate rotation and egress policy changes. We can then send a consolidated workbook and a one-page narrative for your audit team.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect — Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

Folks — I reviewed Marissa's draft attachments and added CAIQ/SIG mapping notes in column D of the workbook. A few technical clarifications to include in the final narrative: 

1) Control-plane ingress: management connections are TLS mutual-authenticating and originate from our control proxies; we maintain a signed cert per customer in KMS and rotate quarterly. Include rotation cadence and the KMS key ARNs in the workbook.
2) Telemetry egress: telemetry aggregation endpoints are routed through an outbound proxy with enforced allowlist. We should call out tokenized telemetry (no PII) and retention window (30 days default, configurable up to 365 days for enterprise).
3) Hardware/host boundary: Dedicated GPU pools can be isolated by host-pinning in our pool manager; call out that Dedicated customers can request NVLink-disabled host profiles to reduce cross-tenant memory sharing risk.

I'll attach a short excerpt from our ops runbook (certificate rotation steps) and a small ACL sample. Marissa — if you send to Javier after I merge, I'll sign off.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Manager, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BlueRiver - control fence playbook + CAIQ/SIG evidence routing (final pack)

Javier — attached is the consolidated pack. Key callouts in the one-page narrative: 

- Audit logs: control-plane and data-plane audit logs are retained in our encrypted logging bucket; standard retention is 90 days for hosted telemetry, 365 days for Dedicated customers under enterprise contracts. Logs are write-once and accessible to the customer on request via signed export (S3 presigned link) and via our console; Redwoods' SOC 2 internal access is limited to a narrow ops group with justification-based access requests.
- External endpoints: the control proxies call a small set of endpoints for telemetry ingestion, runtime updates, and certificate revocation checks. The list is included in the workbook (column F) and contains FQDNs and destination IP ranges; we provide an allowlist export for customers to paste into their firewall rules.
- Evidence index: the workbook references specific artefacts by name and location (diagram v2, playbook v1, runbook excerpt). For SIG reviewers we've also annotated each CAIQ question with where to find the supporting artifact.

Attachments in this message: redwood-control-fence-playbook-v1.pdf; network-diagram-tenant-overlay-v2.png; sig-responses-compiled-BlueRiver.xlsx.
